title: Comparative judgment protocol + NDCG audit for rerank onboarding
body:
Summary:
This doc defines a comparative-judgment style annotation protocol and the downstream NDCG auditing pipeline for reranker model onboarding. It's intended for model owners, applied ML engineers, and annotators running evaluation sets during onboarding/regression checks.

Purpose and scope:
- Purpose: produce a high-quality, reproducible reranking evaluation that combines pairwise preference labels with a deterministic mapping to relevance scores for NDCG calculations and slice-based regression detection.
- Scope: offline eval sets used during model onboarding (hosted + dedicated + private variants). Not intended to replace live-safety checks or user-traffic A/B experiments.

High-level approach:
1) Create candidate pairs (A,B) sampled across traffic and synthetic prompts.
2) Collect redundant pairwise preferences (3+ labelers per pair) with tie option and calibration tasks.
3) Convert pairwise preferences into per-item relevance scores using a simple aggregated scoring rule (preferred_count / total_votes) then map to discrete relevance bins for NDCG.
4) Compute NDCG@k overall and per-slice, with bootstrap confidence intervals and paired significance tests vs baseline.

Sampling strategy (how to pick pairs):
- Mix of production-tile samples (70%) and curated hard-negatives (30%). Production samples stratified by: query frequency (head/torso/tail), vertical tag, and user-intent bucket (informational/transactional/navigational).
- Pair construction: for each query, take top-10 candidate ranking from the model-under-test and sample pairs at different rank offsets: (1,2), (1,5), (2,6), (3,10), and some distant pairs (1,20) when available. Also include pairs where candidate sources differ (model-A vs model-B) for direct model-vs-model comparisons.
- Target dataset size: ~6k unique queries -> ~30k pairs (configurable).

Annotation UI & labeling instructions (copy for the annotator UI):
You will be shown a query and two candidate results (A and B). Choose the option that you believe is more helpful to the user given the query.
- Options: A preferred | B preferred | Tie | Insufficient information (flag)
- Preference guidance: focus on usefulness for the stated intent, correctness of facts, relevance, and completeness. Prefer shorter, direct answers for navigational queries; prefer more context for informational queries.
- Ties: use sparingly, only when both candidates are equivalently helpful or both missing critical info.
- Insufficient information: use if the pair cannot be judged because both are truncated or obviously corrupted.
- Time per judgment: target 20–45s.

Quality control (QC):
- Redundancy: 3 labelers per pair by default. If the 3-way votes are 2-1, accept majority. If 3-way has all distinct (A/B/Tie) escalate to adjudication (2 additional labelers + lead adjudicator).
- Honeypots: 5% of pairs are seeded "gold" with an obvious correct answer (derived from earlier adjudicated sets). Failure rate > 15% for a labeler triggers review and potential removal.
- Calibration tasks: each annotator sees 10 calibration pairs before starting; performance must be >=80% on known calibration labels.
- Labeler profile fields collected: experience_level, language_fluency, annotation_time_median, recent_accuracy. Use to detect drift.

Label encoding and mapping into relevance scores (deterministic rules):
- Raw vote aggregation: for each item (document) associated with the query, compute preferred_count and tie_count across all pairs that include the item for that query.
- Normalized preference score S_item := (preferred_count + 0.5 * tie_count) / total_votes_for_item. This yields 0..1.
- Convert S_item to discrete relevance bins for NDCG mapping. Default mapping (configurable):
  - S >= 0.85 -> rel=3 (Highly relevant)
  - 0.60 <= S < 0.85 -> rel=2 (Relevant)
  - 0.35 <= S < 0.60 -> rel=1 (Somewhat)
  - S < 0.35 -> rel=0 (Not relevant)
- Rationale: pairwise preferences are not absolute grades; the quantile thresholds reduce noise from sparse counts. We recommend inspecting distribution per dataset and adjusting thresholds.

Alternative scoring options (notes):
- Bradley-Terry (BT) or TrueSkill can be used if pair graph coverage is dense; BT yields continuous latent relevances and can be used instead of the simple normalized S_item mapping. BT is more robust to sparse pair graphs but requires an additional model training step.

NDCG computation & bootstrap CI pipeline:
- Compute DCG@k using rel values above and log2 discounting: DCG = sum_{i=1..k} (2^{rel_i}-1)/log2(i+1).
- Ideal DCG computed from sorting by rel desc. NDCG = DCG/IDCG. Compute at k=1,3,5,10 by default.
- Bootstrap CI: resample queries with replacement 1000 times, compute NDCG per resample, report 95% CI (2.5/97.5 percentiles).
- Paired bootstrap test: to compare two models (A vs B), resample queries and compute difference in NDCG for each resample; p-value = fraction of resamples with difference <= 0 for a one-sided test (model A better than B).

Tie handling details in NDCG mapping:
- Ties in pairwise votes lower S_item; ties are weighted 0.5 to avoid inflating both items. Alternative: treat ties as missing and rely on other pairs. We default to 0.5.

Regression detection rules (alert thresholds):
- Primary signal: delta NDCG@5 (new_model - baseline) < -0.003 with p < 0.05 -> soft warning.
- Hard fail: delta NDCG@5 < -0.01 and p < 0.01.
- Secondary signals: increases in pairwise inversion rate (fraction of pairs where baseline preferred over new_model) > 2% absolute and drop in head-query NDCG@5 > 0.007.
- Additionally flag any new model that improves overall NDCG but shows regressions on a critical slice (security/privacy/legal queries or high-value intents).

Slice analysis (how slices are defined and used):
- Default slices created for all eval runs: query-frequency (head/torso/tail), length (short <=3, mid 4-8, long >8 tokens), ambiguity (high/low; defined by labeler agreement <60% => high), recency-sensitive (queries with time filters), vertical (qa/docs/code/product), and traffic-value (high/med/low revenue buckets).
- Compute NDCG@k and bootstrap CI per slice. If slice size < 50 queries, report but treat p-values as unreliable.
- Slice importance ranking: compute "slice impact" = |delta NDCG| * slice_query_share. Use to prioritize investigations.

Adjudication workflow:
- Trigger: any pair where initial 3 votes produce no majority OR where the pair is part of a flagged slice + model delta triggers.
- Process: 2 senior annotators re-annotate -> if they agree, their label stands. If still disagreement, lead annotator adjudicates and writes a short rationale in adjudication_notes field.
- Keep adjudicated labels separate so we can compute metrics with/without adjudication.

Sanity checks & known pitfalls:
- Correlated errors: if many pairs include the same corrupted candidate (e.g., hallucinated block), pairwise aggregation can over-estimate that candidate's score. Detect by per-doc vote concentration (if an item appears in >30 pairs and has inconsistent votes, mark for manual review).
- Prompt leakage: ensure prompt text is not present in candidate doc_texts; if prompt echo appears, add filter.
- Inconsistent prompt variants: keep prompt_variant metadata so we can stratify.

Outputs and artifacts produced for each run:
- pairs.csv: columns -> sample_id, query, doc_id_A, doc_text_A, doc_id_B, doc_text_B, prompt_variant, source, rank_A, rank_B, model_version_A, model_version_B, pair_id.
- raw_votes.csv: pair_id, labeler_id, vote (A|B|Tie|Insufficient), time_seconds, is_gold (y/n).
- aggregated_relevance.csv: query, doc_id, S_item, rel_bin, votes_total, votes_pref, votes_tie.
- ndcg_report.csv: metrics (NDCG@1,3,5,10), bootstrap_mean, ci_lower, ci_upper, model_tag, baseline_tag, run_id.
- slice_report.csv: slice_name, slice_size, NDCG@5_new, NDCG@5_base, delta, p_value, impact_score.

Example lines (pairs.csv style):
- sample_id: q-202501-0001, query: "how to rotate image in python", doc_id_A: m1-d345, doc_text_A: "Use PIL.Image.rotate(...)", doc_id_B: m1-d678, doc_text_B: "Use cv2.getRotationMatrix2D(...) and cv2.warpAffine(...)", prompt_variant: "code-qa-v1", model_version_A: "rerank-v2", model_version_B: "rerank-v2", pair_id: p-00001
- raw_votes.csv example: p-00001, labeler_322, A, 21, n

Reporting checklist for onboarding PRs:
- include full ndcg_report.csv and slice_report.csv + top 20 pairs where models disagreed and at least one side was adjudicated.
- include labeler QoE summary (median time, accuracy on honeypots).
- flag any small-sample slices (<50) in the PR and propose next steps (collect more pairs or accept low-power warning).

Quick-run diagnostics for engineers (commands):
- Recompute aggregated relevance locally: python tools/agg_preferences.py --raw raw_votes.csv --out aggregated_relevance.csv --mapping-bins default
- Compute NDCG + bootstrap: python tools/ndcg_bootstrap.py --agg aggregated_relevance.csv --k 5 --resamples 1000 --out ndcg_report.csv
- Slice report: python tools/slice_analysis.py --pairs pairs.csv --agg aggregated_relevance.csv --slices config/slices.yaml --out slice_report.csv

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Validate default S_item->rel bin thresholds across 3 historical evals; consider adaptive quantile mapping per-run.
- Decide whether to adopt Bradley-Terry by default for runs with >80% pair coverage.
- Define stricter thresholds for critical slices (security/legal).

Appendix: example adjudication note template:
- pair_id: p-0456
- query: "is X compatible with Y"
- summary: "Candidate A gave a short yes/no; candidate B included version matrix with nuance. Senior annotator marked B preferred due to coverage of compatibility matrix. Adjudicator: B preferred (rel=2)."

End of doc.
